title: Vibration-Accelerated Corrosion: Coupled Mechano-Electrochemical Simulation (Integrity Code Series Bonus)
description:
Physics-first engineering simulation of vibration-accelerated corrosion in X65 carbon-steel pipe under CO2-saturated brine at low-cycle pipe-support contacts. The model couples four mechanisms:

  1. Damped single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) structural vibration
  2. Stress-modified Butler-Volmer electrochemical kinetics (anodic dissolution accelerated by activation-volume term)
  3. Faraday mass-loss conversion to corrosion rate
  4. Archard fretting wear at support contacts

A Gradient-Boosted Regression surrogate is trained on 50,000+ physics-generated data points for real-time deployment. Bonus entry in the Integrity Code Series. Limitations are documented explicitly: stress-activation coefficient is phenomenological, fretting-corrosion synergy term is not modeled, and the pH model uses a Nernst approximation only.
references: Archard J.F. (1953). Contact and rubbing of flat surfaces. Journal of Applied Physics 24(8): 981-988.
Nesic S. (2007). Key issues related to modelling of internal corrosion of oil and gas pipelines. Corrosion Science 49: 4308-4338.
Larsen-Basse J. (1973). Wear of hard-metals in rock drilling. Wear 24(3): 263-275.
ISO 21457:2010. Materials selection and corrosion control for oil and gas production systems.
